svg.text: add-app — the seven ordered steps that produce a compliant app tree
Creates the Kustomize base, both overlays, and an Argo CD Application for one app. Each step gates the next.
.kiro/skills/add-app/SKILL.md · the skill Lab C's thin prompt actually runs
matched from the skill's own description field, not chosen by the user
"add a new app" · "create a new service" · "onboard a workload" · "add a cluster overlay to an existing app" · "deploy something new through Argo CD"
Lab C's prompt — Add a web-service app named demo-nginx — matches the first of these, which is why one sentence is enough to start the whole procedure.
Moving an app off existing infrastructure? Run migrate-workload instead — it covers discovery, containerisation, and identity, then calls back into this workflow at its Phase 5.
the gate that protects every later step
Create no files until the archetype and its required fields are known. Scaffolding around a guess produces a tree that has to be unpicked rather than edited.
Always ask for: app_name · archetype · a source image (Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR, local build — wherever it currently lives)
Then archetype-specific fields from the workload archetypes steering file, plus secrets, egress destinations, and whether the app needs an Ingress.
Everything else comes from the project profile rather than from a question — that is what makes the prompt thin.
Both overlays are always created. Do not ask which cluster — there is no valid answer other than "both".
the source registry is an input; ECR is what gets deployed
repository is managed elsewhere — assume it already exists, do not create it
Source is already that ECR repo
Record its digest and continue. Nothing to move.
1. Pull the source image 2. Retag to the ECR path above and push 3. Record the digest
Image not pushed yet, so no real digest exists? Use the 64-hex dummy so the scaffold still passes validation:
Never write docker.io/... , ghcr.io/... , or any other upstream registry into the manifests. Manifests only ever reference the project ECR.
what is identical across both clusters
Argo CD Application using the profile defaults
For plain-manifest apps base/manifests/ holds serviceaccount.yaml,
networkpolicy.yaml, and the workload, with its own kustomization.yaml.
Workloads / SA / NetPol / pod app.kubernetes.io/name · owner
Floating tag here; overlay digests pin the same repository.

networkpolicy.yaml must include default-deny-all plus one allow per required flow (DNS always; HTTPS / Pod Identity / SSH / ingress as needed). Every container declares explicit CPU and memory requests and limits.
web-service: readiness and liveness probes on every HTTP container. Deployment rolling update defaults to maxUnavailable: 0 / maxSurge: 1.
PDB only when replicas (or KEDA/HPA min) is >= 2. Never add minAvailable: 1 while replicas: 1 — it causes DisruptionBlocked on node replacement.
both are required — never scaffold one and leave prod for promotion time
Rewrites source.path to this overlay's manifests/
Overlay patches cover exactly four things
the pinned image digest · replica count or scaling bounds ·
Start prod as a copy of dev
and change only what genuinely differs.
Digest unknown at scaffold time? Use the 64-hex dummy — ...0001 dev / ...0002 prod. These pass gator test --deny-only but are not deployable.
Never write REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_DIGEST — it fails the disallowed-tags constraint. Replace with the real digest after pushing to ECR.
Any annotation carrying an AWS account ID belongs in the overlay
dev and prod are separate accounts, so these ARNs always differ
No ARNs, no hostnames, no account IDs.
TLS is overlay-specific too — the hostname differs per environment.
Never write bare tokens like REPLACE_WITH_CERT_ID or REPLACE_WITH_WEBACL_ID — they fail Gatekeeper validation offline and in CI. The dummies above match the WAFv2 and ACM ARN regexes, so they pass.
copy the shape from identity-and-secrets steering, then narrow it
Holds the IAM policy and the Pod Identity association. Fill <app> / <cluster>, then replace the policy statement with what the app actually calls.
Explicit actions, explicit resource ARNs. This is the step the factory deliberately does not automate — scoping a role is a judgement call.
Using a SecretProviderClass? The policy must include
(+ kms:Decrypt if CMK-encrypted), scoped to those ARNs.

text.tspan: App calls no AWS APIs and has no secrets?

svg.text: It still needs a ServiceAccount, but no iam.tf at all.
Purpose, then ## Inputs and outputs with a Mermaid flowchart LR: inputs / workers / outputs subgraphs and
labeled edges derived from real config, tables under the diagram, then image / IAM / networking as needed.
Digest bump config for the overlay pin
files, if the repo uses Renovate.
Extend it from the root config.
the gate that decides whether the scaffold is actually done
for c in dev-eks-1 prod-eks-1; do
Whatever policy_engine is set to. Validate against
expanded Pod templates, not the controller manifests alone.
An admission failure surfaces as an Argo CD sync sitting
in a degraded state — a much slower way to learn about a
Base first, then both overlays and their manifests/ — so a base-level error surfaces before either overlay is touched.
All green? The scaffold is done. Commit, open a PR, and let a human review it.
Rolling out — after the PR merges
the skill stops at the PR; everything below is a human decision
Only then promote the digest to prod
Order matters: Terraform before manifests when adding a permission, and always reach dev-eks-1 before prod-eks-1 — see the GitOps conventions map.
gather inputs → resolve the image → scaffold base → scaffold both overlays → declare IAM → supporting files → validate → PR → human review
